[2, 4, 5] This major gift is intended to accelerate research toward developing a biological cure for type 1 diabetes (T1D). [2, 5] The announcement was made at a "Decades of Discoveries" reception celebrating over 50 years of the DRI's contributions to diabetes research. [6] This donation establishes the DRI Foundation as one of the largest donors in the University of Miami's history, with total support exceeding $270 million. [6] The funding will also support the work of the DRI's new scientific director, world-renowned immunologist Dr. Matthias von Herrath. [3, 5] <2> UC Davis Medical Center was recognized as one of the nation's top hospitals for diabetes and endocrinology, securing a tie for the 33rd position in the U.S. News & World Report's 2023-2024 Best Hospitals survey. In addition to this national ranking, the medical center's diabetes care was rated as 'High Performing,' which is the highest possible rating for common adult procedures and conditions. <3> On July 20, 2023, the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), a component of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), officially announced a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) under the identifier RFA-HL-24-008. [1, 12] The initiative, titled "The Role of Sleep Deficiency in Persons with Type 1 Diabetes: Sleep, Glycemic Control, and Cardiovascular Risk," seeks to support research elucidating how sleep deficiency and circadian disruption contribute to metabolic and cardiovascular issues in individuals with Type 1 Diabetes. [1, 2] This NOFO encourages the formation of multi-disciplinary research teams that bridge the fields of sleep/circadian science, diabetes, and cardiovascular research to investigate the underlying mechanisms of these relationships. [1, 2] <4> Tandem Diabetes Care announced on July 11, 2023, that it had received U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) clearance for its Mobi insulin pump for individuals with diabetes aged six and older. [1, 2, 3] The company describes the Mobi as the world's smallest durable automated insulin delivery (AID) system, being less than half the size of its t:slim X2 pump. [1, 5] The pump is fully controllable via a mobile app on a compatible iPhone and integrates with Tandem's Control-IQ technology. [2, 3] This algorithm predicts glucose levels 30 minutes in advance using data from a compatible continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and automatically adjusts insulin delivery every five minutes to help prevent high and low blood sugar. [2, 3] It can also deliver automatic correction boluses. [2] The Mobi system features a 200-unit insulin cartridge and a physical button on the pump for manual insulin boluses as an alternative to phone control. [5] A limited U.S. release was planned for late 2023, with a full commercial launch anticipated in early 2024. [1, 2, 4] Developed by CellTrans Inc., the therapy uses pancreatic cells from deceased donors and is intended for adults with 'brittle' type 1 diabetes who are unable to reach target blood glucose levels because of recurring, severe hypoglycemic events despite intensive management. [1, 2, 5] The approval was based on the safety and effectiveness demonstrated in two single-arm studies involving a total of 30 participants. [3] In these trials, 21 participants achieved insulin independence for a year or longer, with 11 remaining insulin-free for one to five years and 10 for more than five years. [3, 4] <6> The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved two medications, Jardiance (empagliflozin) and Synjardy (empagliflozin and metformin hydrochloride), to improve blood sugar control in children aged 10 and older with type 2 diabetes. [1] This approval, announced on June 20, 2023, makes a new class of oral medications available for this pediatric population, intended for use as an adjunct to diet and exercise. [1, 6] Prior to this, metformin was the only oral therapy approved for children with type 2 diabetes, a milestone that occurred in 2000. [1, 7] The approval of Jardiance, an SGLT2 inhibitor, and Synjardy was based on a clinical trial involving 157 patients aged 10 to 17, which demonstrated that empagliflozin was effective at reducing hemoglobin A1c levels compared to a placebo. [3, 7] Side effects in children were generally similar to those in adults, though a higher risk of hypoglycemia was noted. [6, 8] <7> The American Diabetes Association (ADA) held its 83rd Scientific Sessions in a hybrid format, with the in-person event taking place in San Diego, California, from June 23-26, 2023. The conference, which convened over 12,000 participants, featured more than 190 sessions and 2,000 original research presentations. Key discussions and findings centered on new medications for type 2 diabetes and obesity, such as high-dose oral semaglutide and the GIP/GLP-1/glucagon receptor triple agonist, retatrutide. The program also covered advancements in diabetes technology, including debates on DIY versus commercial automated insulin delivery systems, and strategies for prevention, particularly immunotherapies for type 1 diabetes. <8> The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a warning to consumers on May 30, 2023, regarding the risks associated with compounded versions of semaglutide. [1, 3] This action was prompted by reports of adverse events and the ongoing shortages of FDA-approved semaglutide products like Ozempic and Wegovy, which has led some pharmacies to create compounded alternatives. [1, 6] The FDA explicitly stated that it does not review these compounded drugs for safety, effectiveness, or quality. [1] A significant concern highlighted in the warning is that some compounders may be using salt forms of semaglutide, such as semaglutide sodium and semaglutide acetate. These are different active ingredients from the one used in the approved medications, and the FDA is not aware of any basis for their use in compounding that would meet federal requirements. [6] <9> Vertex Pharmaceuticals' investigational stem cell-derived therapy for type 1 diabetes, VX-880, was granted PRIME (PRIority MEdicines) designation by the European Medicines Agency in March 2023. [1, 3, 4] This designation is designed to enhance support for the development of medicines that target a significant unmet medical need. [1, 3] The therapy, which aims to restore the body's ability to regulate glucose by replacing destroyed pancreatic islet cells, is being evaluated in a Phase 1/2 clinical trial for patients with type 1 diabetes, impaired hypoglycemic awareness, and severe hypoglycemic events. [1, 2] The granting of the PRIME designation was officially reported in the company's first-quarter financial results. [4]

[1, 3] Eli Lilly announced that Zepbound was expected to be available in the U.S. by the end of 2023. The legislation was reintroduced by Senators Gary Peters (D-MI) and Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV) during National Diabetes Month. The primary goal of the bill is to amend Title XVIII of the Social Security Act to extend Medicare coverage for medical nutrition therapy (MNT) services to beneficiaries who have pre-diabetes or are at risk for developing type-2 diabetes. Currently, Medicare only covers these services for individuals already diagnosed with diabetes or renal disease. Supporters, including the American Diabetes Association and the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics, argue that the bill could improve health outcomes for millions, reduce the number of new diabetes cases, and lower long-term healthcare costs for Medicare. <5> A study published in Cell Reports Medicine suggests that the repurposed drug α-difluoromethylornithine (DFMO) shows potential for managing type 1 diabetes. Research led by Indiana University School of Medicine and the University of Chicago Medicine indicated that DFMO, an FDA-approved drug, could preserve the function of insulin-producing beta cells, potentially reducing a patient's dependency on insulin injections. The study, which builds on over a decade of research, involved a randomized controlled trial with 41 subjects recently diagnosed with type 1 diabetes. The results found that DFMO was safe, well-tolerated, and at higher doses, preserved C-peptide levels, a marker for insulin production, without significant immunomodulation. Following these promising findings, a larger, multi-center clinical trial has been launched to further evaluate the efficacy of DFMO in treating type 1 diabetes. <6> Researchers from the Diabetes Research Institute (DRI) at the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine have developed a groundbreaking technique for the dynamic analysis of pancreatic regeneration in type 1 diabetes, with findings published on October 27, 2023. [2] This new method allows scientists to culture live sections of a human pancreas for nearly two weeks, preserving the organ's cellular architecture and cell-to-cell interactions. [2] Using this technique, they created the first-ever dynamic single-cell map of the pancreas's regenerative pathways. [2] The study, published in the journal *Cell Metabolism*, revealed that a growth factor, BMP-7, can stimulate pancreatic stem-like cells to become new insulin-producing beta cells, even in tissue from donors with type 1 diabetes. [2] This breakthrough provides a unique model to study pancreatic regeneration and paves the way for potential pharmacological treatments that could help the pancreas heal itself. [2] <7> In observance of National Diabetes Month and World Diabetes Day in November 2023, the American Diabetes Association (ADA) convened a series of 'State of Diabetes' events across the United States. According to the ADA's 2023 annual report, there were 19 such events held. These gatherings brought together community members, businesses, healthcare professionals, and industry leaders to evaluate the current landscape of diabetes and find solutions to improve care and support. Confirmed events included a conference in Daytona Beach, Florida, on November 11, 2023, in partnership with Halifax Health; a breakfast in Houston, Texas, on November 13, 2023; a health expo in Durham, North Carolina, on November 18, 2023, with Durham Technical Community College; and an event in Boston on November 3, 2023. The initiative aimed to address the significant personal and financial burdens of the diabetes epidemic by combining ADA resources with local expertise to enhance support and care. <8> On October 5, 2023, the Diabetes Research Institute Foundation (DRIF) announced a significant $50 million commitment to the Diabetes Research Institute (DRI) at the University of Miami Miller School of Medicine. [2, 4, 5] This major gift is intended to accelerate research toward developing a biological cure for type 1 diabetes (T1D). [2, 5] The announcement was made at a "Decades of Discoveries" reception celebrating over 50 years of the DRI's contributions to diabetes research. [6] This donation establishes the DRI Foundation as one of the largest donors in the University of Miami's history, with total support exceeding $270 million. [6] The funding will also support the work of the DRI's new scientific director, world-renowned immunologist Dr. Matthias von Herrath. [3, 5]
